_meta.title: StyleSync AI — Virtual Try-On Workflow
_meta.description: ComfyUI workflow for garment-to-model generation with logo preservation

1_load_garment.comment: Load the flat-lay garment image (background already removed)

2_load_pose.comment: Load OpenPose skeleton or reference model photo

4_openpose_preprocessor.comment: Extract OpenPose skeleton from reference model image

5_canny_preprocessor.comment: Extract garment edges — helps preserve texture boundaries and logo outlines

inputs.text: professional ecommerce product photo, fashion model wearing the exact garment, facing the camera directly, clean white studio background, soft diffused studio lighting, high resolution, 8k, sharp details, accurate fabric texture and color reproduction, garment logo perfectly preserved

9_clip_text_positive.comment: Positive prompt — dynamically populated by the agent based on RAG style guidelines

inputs.text: blurry, low quality, deformed, distorted, extra limbs, bad anatomy, watermark, text overlay, garment color changed, wrong fabric texture, logo distorted, logo removed, logo color changed

10_clip_text_negative.comment: Negative prompt — includes logo protection hints from RAG

11_apply_controlnet_pose.comment: Apply pose ControlNet — high strength for accurate body positioning

12_apply_controlnet_canny.comment: Apply canny ControlNet — moderate strength to preserve garment edges and logo boundaries

13_ip_adapter_loader.comment: IP-Adapter for garment texture/color transfer from the input image

14_ip_adapter_apply.comment: Transfer garment appearance — weight 0.7 balances fidelity vs. flexibility

15_ksampler_base.comment: Base generation — 30 steps with DPM++ 2M Karras scheduler

17_logo_composite.comment: KEY STEP: Composite the original logo region back onto the generated image using the mask. This ensures pixel-perfect logo preservation regardless of generation quality.

18_inpaint_refine.comment: Light refinement pass — low denoise (0.3) to blend the composited logo seamlessly without altering it

logo_preservation_strategy: 1. Canny ControlNet extracts garment edges including logo boundaries
2. IP-Adapter transfers garment texture/color from input flat-lay
3. After base generation, the original logo region is composited back using a binary mask
4. A light refinement pass (denoise=0.3) blends the seams without altering the logo
5. The logo mask should have ~10px feathered edges for seamless blending
texture_consistency_tips: IP-Adapter weight 0.7 is optimal — lower loses texture, higher causes artifacts
Canny ControlNet at 0.5 strength preserves fabric patterns without over-constraining
Use the same seed across variants for consistent model appearance
For striped/patterned garments, increase Canny strength to 0.65
